load_order.reason: Foundational object. Holds default values (Inventory Source, Eng Type, Lot/Serial Tracking, Planning Policy, costing weights, lead times, etc.) that propagate to Engineering Item Master records via the rstk__peitem_iccomcod__r external ID foreign key. Must exist in Rootstock before any peitem record can reference it.

Every peitem record requires a valid iccomcod external ID via rstk__peitem_iccomcod__r. Loading peitem before iccomcod will cause every row to fail validation on the FK lookup. Per the peitem schema doc: 'The Inventory Commodity Code record must exist before adding the Engineering Item Master for the respective Inventory Division.'

entries.explanation: A label that appears on the first row of each assembly in the BoM, formatted as '<Assembly>-<CaseQuantity>' (for example, 'P-DWS-1000' indicates the P-DWS assembly with 1,000 units per case). Despite the name, this is not a Rootstock commodity code — it is a header marker used by the source system. The information it carries is already available in Assy Item and ProductCaseQty.
transformations: No transformation needed — this field is not loaded. If desired, parse the case quantity portion (the suffix after the last hyphen) and use it to cross-validate against ProductCaseQty in the Products table.

entries.explanation:
Field type: Lookup(Inventory Commodity Code), External ID, Required.

Drives commodity code routing for raw materials and components that exist in the BoM but not in the Products catalog (~68 items: inks, glues, paper sheets, boxes, tape). 'Non Inventory' indicates consumables that should not be MRP-planned (inks coded A0xxx, glues coded D0xxx/C0xxx). 'Inventory' indicates stock-tracked raw materials that do need planning (paper PR-*, boxes BX-/BC-/N0-*, stadium cup blanks WSC*).

Note: this BoM field has different semantics from the peitem.Item Type field, which uses Direct Material / Labor Only — the picklists do not align.

External ID format: all outputs prefixed with '2_' (division 2) per schema requirement '<division_external_id>_<commodity_code>'.
transformations:
Apply only to SKUs that appear as BoM.Part # but not as Products.ProductSKU:

  WHEN BoM.Item Type = 'Non Inventory':
    IF Part # matches /^A\d{4}/                          → '2_RCB-CONSUMABLE-INK'
    IF Part # matches /^D\d{4}|^C\d{4}/                  → '2_RCB-CONSUMABLE-GLUE'  (D0001, C0026 etc. — glues, not inks)
    IF Part # matches /^H\d{4}|TAPE|LABEL/ OR = 'BCI'    → '2_RCB-PACKAGING'         (BCI = printed instructions)
    ELSE                                                  → '2_RCB-UNROUTED'         (explicit catch-all, requires human review)

  WHEN BoM.Item Type = 'Inventory':
    IF Part # LIKE 'PR-%' OR contains 'SBS'/'KRA'         → '2_RCB-PRINT-MAT'        (paper raw material)
    IF Part # LIKE 'BX-%'/'BG-%'/'S-%'/'BC%'/'N0%'        → '2_RCB-PACKAGING'        (boxes, bags incl. BCB-*/BCK-*/BCW-*/N0068)
    IF Part # LIKE 'WSC%'                                 → '2_RCB-BLANK-CUP'        (stadium cup blanks WSC22/WSC32)
    ELSE                                                  → '2_RCB-UNROUTED'         (explicit catch-all, requires human review)

All outputs prefixed with '2_' (division 2). Items routed to RCB-UNROUTED must be reviewed by the user before load — silent fallback to a default category is not used.

entries.explanation:
Field type: Text(50), Required.

Each distinct Assy Item is a manufactured assembly that should become one Engineering Item Master record with Inventory Source = Manufactured. The BoM contains 1,562 rows but only 123 unique parent assemblies — duplicates collapse on distinct extraction. After whitespace trimming, all 123 Assy Items match a corresponding Products.ProductSKU.
transformations: Take distinct trimmed values of Assy Item where Assy Item is not null. When merging with Products.ProductSKU extraction: SKUs that exist in both sources keep Inventory Source = Manufactured (a SKU with a BoM is manufactured regardless of catalog presence), but Products.ProductName wins for Item Description because it is more complete (4,587 catalog descriptions vs 123 BoM descriptions).

entries.explanation: Restates information already available elsewhere — combines Assy Item with the case-size description, for example 'P-DWS, 1 Case (1000 Sleeves)'. The same content can be reconstructed from Assy Item plus ProductCaseQty.
transformations: No transformation needed — this field is not loaded.

entries.explanation:
Field type: Text(100), Required.

Description for parent assemblies, repeated identically across every component row within an assembly. Used as a fallback when the corresponding SKU has no ProductName in the Products catalog. Products.ProductName is preferred when available because it covers more SKUs (4,587 vs 123) and tends to be more current.
transformations: Take distinct trimmed values of Assy Desc paired with Assy Item. When the same SKU also exists in Products: use COALESCE(Products.ProductName, BoM.Assy_Desc) — Products.ProductName wins when both are present.

entries.explanation:
Field type: Text(50), Required.

Each distinct Part # represents a component used in a BoM that should become its own Engineering Item Master record. About 68 of 125 components exist only in the BoM and not in the Products catalog — these include raw paper (PR-SBS-*), inks (A000x), glues (D0001), boxes (BX-*), and tape. For these items, the BoM is the only source available. Items extracted from Part # default to Inventory Source = Purchased unless they also appear as a BoM parent (Assy Item).
transformations: Take distinct trimmed values of Part # where Part # is not null. Then exclude any value that already exists as an Assy Item (those are manufactured parents — already loaded with Inventory Source = Manufactured) or as a Products.ProductSKU (those come from the catalog instead). Only emit Part # values that no other source already created.

entries.explanation:
Field type: Text(100), Required.

Description for components in the BoM (for example, 'Atlantic 16pt SBS, 23"x29"'). Used only for the ~68 Part # values that don't exist in the Products catalog. When a Part # also appears in Products.ProductSKU, the catalog's ProductName takes priority.
transformations: Trim whitespace. Use only when the Part # has no corresponding Products.ProductName. Final priority for Item Description: Products.ProductName > BoM.Assy_Desc > BoM.Item.

entries.explanation: A binary flag (0.0, 1.0, or null) with unclear semantics in the source data. The actual per-unit consumption quantity is captured in the BoM's Qty field, not here. This field would belong on a BOM Component record (the table that links a parent to its components with quantities), which is a separate target object not included in the current Engineering Item Master and Inventory Commodity Code migration scope.
transformations: No transformation needed for these tables. Preserve this field for the future BOM Component migration phase.

entries.explanation:
Field type: Lookup(Unit of Measure), External ID, Required.

Per-component engineering UOM in the BoM (Sheet, 5Kg, Gallon, Each, Roll, Linear FT, Lbs, Liter). This drives the Eng UOM for components extracted from BoM.Part #. Parent assemblies (finished cups and sleeves) are always counted as Each and use a hardcoded EA value — they don't pull from this field.
transformations:
For components extracted from BoM.Part #, look up the source UOM and map to Rootstock UOM external ID:

  Sheet     → SHEET
  5Kg       → KG    (note: '5Kg' is the pail size, not a unit — confirm with RCB whether inks should be tracked in KG by weight or in pails as Each)
  Gallon    → GAL
  Each      → EA
  Roll      → ROLL
  Linear FT → FT
  Lbs       → LB
  Liter     → L

For parent assemblies extracted from BoM.Assy Item, hardcode EA. Pre-create any missing UOM records in Rootstock before loading peitem rows.

entries.explanation:
Field type: Lookup(Unit of Measure), External ID, Required.

Default engineering UOM at the commodity code level. Items inherit this default unless overridden at the item level. Set once per commodity code, derived from the most common UOM among the items in that code. Manufactured codes (printed cups, sleeves) use EA. Raw-material codes use the source UOM — paper codes use SHEET, ink codes use KG.
transformations:
Group items by their assigned commodity code, take the most common UOM among them, and map to a Rootstock UOM external ID. Per-commodity-code constant. Recommended values for RCB:

  RCB-PRINT-CUP, RCB-PRINT-SLEEVE, RCB-BLANK,
  RCB-STOCK-RESALE, RCB-PACKAGING, RCB-APPAREL-DROP  → EA
  RCB-PRINT-MAT       → SHEET
  RCB-CONSUMABLE-INK  → KG

entries.explanation:
Field type: Lookup(Unit of Measure), External ID, Required.

Default inventory UOM — how RCB tracks stock for items in this commodity code. Reference data shows EA across all codes because cups, sleeves, blanks, boxes, and drop-ship items are all counted in whole units. Override to a bulk unit (KG) only for consumables tracked by weight, such as inks.
transformations:
Default to EA. Override per commodity code only where bulk weight tracking applies:

  RCB-CONSUMABLE-INK → KG
  All other codes    → EA

entries.explanation:
Field type: Lookup(Unit of Measure), External ID, Conditionally Required.

Default purchasing UOM — how RCB buys items in this commodity code. Finished and stock items are purchased in Each. Raw materials and consumables are purchased in their bulk forms (paper by the SHEET, ink by the KG, tape by the ROLL).
transformations:
Group items by commodity code and take the most common purchasing UOM among them. Recommended values:

  RCB-PRINT-CUP, RCB-PRINT-SLEEVE, RCB-BLANK,
  RCB-STOCK-RESALE, RCB-PACKAGING, RCB-APPAREL-DROP  → EA
  RCB-PRINT-MAT       → SHEET
  RCB-CONSUMABLE-INK  → KG

entries.explanation: Per-finished-unit consumption (for example, 0.0625 sheets per sleeve, or 0.00000005 kg of ink per cup). This belongs on the BOM Component record that links a parent to its components with quantities, not on the Engineering Item Master or Inventory Commodity Code tables in the current migration scope.
transformations: No transformation needed for these tables. Preserve this field for the future BOM Component migration phase.

entries.explanation: Per-component cost contribution from the source BoM (for example, $0.02 per sheet). This belongs on Item Cost or BOM Cost records, not on the Engineering Item Master or Inventory Commodity Code tables in the current migration scope.
transformations: No transformation needed for these tables. Preserve this field for the future cost migration phase.

entries.explanation:
Field type: Picklist {Standard, Phantom, Reference}, Optional (inherits from commodity code if blank).

When a component is itself an assembly with its own BoM, the source data flags it as 'Sub-Assembly'. Sub-assemblies that are never independently inventoried should be marked Eng Type = Phantom in Rootstock. Only one SKU (WHC16) carries this flag in the current data, but the rule applies more broadly to any SKU that appears as both a parent and a component if RCB confirms it should be treated as a phantom.
transformations:
Apply this rule when extracting components from BoM.Part #:

  CASE WHEN sub-assembly flag = 'Sub-Assembly' THEN 'Phantom' ELSE 'Standard' END

If a SKU appears as both a parent in one BoM and a sub-assembly component in another, keep Inventory Source = Manufactured but set Eng Type = Phantom. Confirm with RCB whether other multi-BoM SKUs should also be marked Phantom.

entries.explanation: Internal numeric primary key from the source system (Prosys). It has no business meaning outside Prosys and is not needed in Rootstock, which generates its own internal IDs.
transformations: No transformation needed — this field is not loaded. If audit traceability back to Prosys is required, optionally preserve in a custom field.

entries.explanation: Foreign key linking each product to a WooCommerce entry (RCB's e-commerce platform). Relevant only if RCB plans to keep the WooCommerce integration after migration. If not, this field has no destination in Rootstock.
transformations: No transformation needed — this field is not loaded. If RCB intends to maintain the WooCommerce integration, preserve in a custom field for the integration layer to use.

entries.explanation:
Field type: Text(50), Required.

The primary business SKU used across orders, purchase orders, and invoices. Each distinct ProductSKU becomes one Engineering Item Master record. This produces ~4,587 EIM records covering every catalog variant.

**Decision point — EIM grain.** RCB's current production Rootstock org has only 338 EIM records, a curated subset closer to InvMasterSKU grain (~386 unique non-sentinel values). There are two defensible approaches:
  (a) ProductSKU grain (~4,587 EIMs) — the platform's default, treats every catalog variant as a distinct item. Matches the natural grain of products.csv.
  (b) InvMasterSKU grain (~386 EIMs) — matches the prod org pattern. Treats EIM as the underlying inventory item; print/decoration variants live on Salesforce Product, not EIM.
Confidence is reduced (55) to surface this as a decision RCB needs to make. The mapping defaults to ProductSKU grain because it preserves all source rows; switching to InvMasterSKU grain requires remapping the source field on Item Number from ProductSKU to InvMasterSKU (with sentinel filtering).

Additional consideration: ProductSKU has 622 duplicate values across 1,873 rows (32% of file). See the transformation rule for dedup logic.
transformations:
Apply dedup before extracting Item Number:

  WITH ranked AS (
    SELECT ProductSKU, ProductName, InvMasterSKU, ProductActive, ProductUpdated,
           ROW_NUMBER() OVER (
             PARTITION BY TRIM(ProductSKU)
             ORDER BY 
               CASE WHEN InvMasterSKU IS NOT NULL AND InvMasterSKU NOT IN ('NO INVENTORY','OUTSOURCED') THEN 0 ELSE 1 END,
               ProductActive DESC,
               ProductUpdated DESC NULLS LAST
           ) AS rn
    FROM products
  )
  SELECT TRIM(ProductSKU) AS item_number FROM ranked WHERE rn = 1

Tiebreaker priority: (1) rows with real InvMasterSKU win over sentinel/null, (2) active items win over inactive, (3) most recently updated wins. Resolves the 622 duplicate SKUs (1,873 rows = 32% of source).

When merging with BoM-sourced Item Numbers: SKUs that exist as BoM Assy Items keep Inventory Source = Manufactured.

entries.explanation:
Field type: Lookup(Inventory Commodity Code), External ID, Required.

ProductSKU pattern is the primary signal for routing manufactured items to the correct commodity code. The pattern distinguishes:
  - Items starting with 'P-' are printed (RCB decorates the blank)
  - Items without 'P-' prefix that appear as BoM parents are manufactured blanks (RCB cuts/forms the cup/sleeve from raw stock)
Body pattern then picks sleeve vs cup geometry. This rule runs after ProductGroupName edge-case routing (Apparel-Outsource and Warehoused) and before BoM Item Type rules for raw materials.

The same ProductSKU field also feeds Item Number — that is a one-to-many mapping where the same source feeds two target fields via different transformations.

External ID format: per schema doc, the lookup expects '<division_external_id>_<commodity_code>'. Division 2 prefix applied to all values (e.g., '2_RCB-PRINT-CUP').
transformations:
Apply for items in the Products catalog or as BoM parents, after ProductGroupName routing has run:

  WHEN ProductSKU starts with 'P-':
      IF body matches /(DWS|DKS|CWS|CKS|WSC)/  → '2_RCB-PRINT-SLEEVE'
      OTHERWISE                                → '2_RCB-PRINT-CUP'

  WHEN SKU is a BoM Assy Item AND does NOT start with 'P-' (manufactured blank):
      IF body matches /(DWS|DKS|CWS|CKS|WSC)/  → '2_RCB-BLANK-SLEEVE'
      OTHERWISE                                → '2_RCB-BLANK-CUP'  (covers WHC08/12/16/20, CHC*, B-CHC*, etc.)

External ID format follows '<division_external_id>_<commodity_code>'. All outputs prefixed with '2_' (division 2).

entries.explanation:
Field type: Text(100), Required.

Free-text product description from the catalog. This is the primary source of item descriptions in Rootstock because it covers all 4,587 catalog SKUs and tends to be more complete and current than BoM descriptions.
transformations: Trim whitespace. Truncate to Rootstock's Item Description max length. When a SKU has descriptions available from multiple sources, apply this priority: Products.ProductName > BoM.Assy_Desc > BoM.Item.

entries.explanation:
Field type: Lookup(Inventory Commodity Code), External ID, Required.

Product category in the source system, with 18 distinct values such as 20WHC, DWS, Pad, Warehoused, and Apparel-Outsource. For most items the commodity code is determined by SKU pattern rather than this field, but two ProductGroupName values trigger important commodity code routings: 'Apparel-Outsource' routes items to RCB-APPAREL-DROP (Subcontract), and 'Warehoused' routes them to RCB-STOCK-RESALE.
transformations:
Apply this rule first, before SKU-pattern routing:

  WHEN ProductGroupName = 'Apparel-Outsource' → '2_RCB-APPAREL-DROP'
  WHEN ProductGroupName = 'Warehoused'        → '2_RCB-STOCK-RESALE'

For any other ProductGroupName value, fall through to the SKU-pattern rule (ProductSKU → iccomcod) and BoM Item Type rule.

External ID format follows '<division_external_id>_<commodity_code>'. All outputs prefixed with '2_' (division 2).

entries.explanation: Supplier brand name (YBC, PLUS, RCB, or Radix). These are RCB's house brands and supplier identifiers, not Rootstock Vendor records. The field belongs on Vendor, Approved Vendor List, or Vendor Item tables, which are separate target objects not included in the current Engineering Item Master and Inventory Commodity Code migration scope.
transformations: No transformation needed for these tables. Preserve this field for the future Vendor migration phase.

entries.explanation: Last-modified timestamp from the source system. Rootstock maintains its own audit timestamps, so legacy timestamps generally are not useful in the new system.
transformations: No transformation needed — this field is not loaded.

entries.explanation:
Field type: Picklist {Manufactured, Purchased, Subcontract}, Optional (inherits from commodity code if blank).

The inventory key in the source system, with 388 distinct values plus TWO sentinels:
  - 'NO INVENTORY' (376 rows) — items not stock-tracked, typically one-off custom orders
  - 'OUTSOURCED' (1,378 rows / 1,275 unique SKUs) — drop-ship items supplied by external vendors. All filed under ProductGroupName='20WHC' in the source data but are actually apparel (Bayside hoodies, Comfort Colors t-shirts, Gildan tees, Alternative pullovers, Sportsman caps, etc.). The ProductGroupName label is misleading for these items; the real discriminator is InvMasterSKU='OUTSOURCED'.

Combined with BoM presence, this field determines whether an item becomes Manufactured, Purchased, Subcontract, or is filtered out of the migration.
transformations:
Apply this resolution rule (order matters):

  IF SKU appears as a BoM Assy Item
      → Inventory Source = Manufactured
  ELSE IF InvMasterSKU = 'OUTSOURCED'
      → Inventory Source = Subcontract  (catches 1,275 drop-ship apparel SKUs)
  ELSE IF ProductGroupName = 'Apparel-Outsource'
      → Inventory Source = Subcontract  (catches 26 stadium cup SKUs)
  ELSE IF InvMasterSKU is non-null AND ≠ 'NO INVENTORY'
      → Inventory Source = Purchased
  ELSE IF InvMasterSKU = 'NO INVENTORY' AND SKU not used in any BoM
      → Filter out (do not load)

The OUTSOURCED branch runs BEFORE the ProductGroupName check because the OUTSOURCED sentinel is the more reliable signal (1,275 SKUs vs 26 SKUs).

entries.explanation: Number of pieces per case (for example, 1,000 sleeves per case). This is UOM conversion data — it captures the relationship 'X cases = Y eaches' for purchasing and shipping. It belongs on the Rootstock UOM Conversion table, a separate target object not in the current migration scope.
transformations: No transformation needed for these tables. Preserve this field for the future UOM Conversion migration phase.

entries.explanation: The selling unit of measure (Case, Single, or Roll). In Rootstock, inventory and engineering UOMs are always EA for these items — the Case and Roll relationships belong on UOM Conversion and Sales Order tables, not on the item master. Do not conflate this with the engineering UOM.
transformations: No transformation needed for these tables. Preserve this field for the future UOM Conversion and Sales Order migration phases.

entries.explanation: Print-shop specific count, likely capturing sheets per case or imposition information. There is no corresponding standard field in the Engineering Item Master or Inventory Commodity Code templates.
transformations: No transformation needed — this field is not loaded. If RCB needs this information after migration, add a custom field to the import template.

entries.explanation: Related to ProductSheets — print-shop math specific to the source system. No standard target field exists in Rootstock.
transformations: No transformation needed — this field is not loaded.

entries.explanation: Numeric foreign key to a product-group lookup in the source system. The relationship between ProductGroupId and ProductGroupName is many-to-many in the source (the same ID can have multiple names, and the same name can have multiple IDs), making this field unreliable for category mapping. Use ProductGroupName instead.
transformations: No transformation needed — this field is not loaded.

entries.explanation: Free-text notes. About 30% of rows are null, and most non-null values are whitespace. No standard Notes field exists on the Engineering Item Master import template.
transformations: No transformation needed — this field is not loaded. If RCB wants to preserve notes, add a custom long-text field to peitem and extend the import template.

entries.explanation:
Field type: Picklist {Pending, Active}, Required.

Lifecycle status of the item. Reference data shows Status values of Active and Pending. In Rootstock, Status and Inactive Status are orthogonal: Status represents the record lifecycle (Active = released, Pending = draft), while Inactive Status represents the usage flag. Inactive items typically keep Status = Active and gain an Inactive Status code; see the Inactive Status mapping for that flag.
transformations: For items sourced from the Products catalog, set Status = 'Active' regardless of the ProductActive value (the active/inactive distinction is handled by Inactive Status). Use 'Pending' only if RCB has a specific convention for items not yet released. For items sourced only from the BoM with no catalog match, default to Status = 'Active'.

entries.explanation:
Field type: Checkbox, Optional (Checked = Inactive; Unchecked = Active or Pending).

Checkbox indicating whether an item is currently in use. Status and Inactive Status are orthogonal: Status is the record lifecycle (Active vs Pending), Inactive Status is the usage flag (FALSE/unchecked = in use, TRUE/checked = retired). The combination Status='Active' with Inactive Status=TRUE represents a legacy item that was once released but is no longer in use — the standard end-of-life state.

Field type caveat: the schema doc shows Checkbox (TRUE/FALSE). The reference template CSV shows a literal 'I' value in this column for an inactive row, suggesting the field may actually accept a single-character code in some org configurations. The transformation uses TRUE/FALSE per the schema; if the live RCB org rejects boolean values, switch to 'I'/blank.
transformations:
Apply this rule only to items sourced from the Products catalog:

  CASE WHEN Products.ProductActive = 0 THEN TRUE ELSE FALSE END

Items sourced only from the BoM (no catalog match) default to FALSE (active). The field is a Checkbox in Rootstock — values are TRUE (checked = inactive) or FALSE / blank (unchecked = active or pending).

entries.explanation:
Field type: Lookup(Division Master), External ID, Required.

Engineering Division FK — assigns the peitem to a division.
transformations: Constant `2` for all peitems (single-division setup per RCB cleaned file).

entries.explanation:
Field type: Lookup(Division Master), External ID, Required.

Inventory Division FK — where stock physically lives. Can differ from Eng Division.
transformations: Constant `2` (same as Eng Division for single-division setup).

entries.explanation:
Field type: Picklist {Blank, Direct Material, Labor Only}, Optional (default Direct Material).

Item kind on peitem (Direct Material / Labor Only). NOTE: Different concept from BoM.Item Type (Inventory/Non Inventory) — picklists do not align.
transformations: Constant `Direct Material` for all peitems (no labor-only items in RCB data).

entries.explanation:
Field type: Lookup(Manufacturing Users), External ID, Required.

Responsible engineer FK (user record). Required even if RCB does not formally track engineering ownership.
transformations: Constant placeholder user ID (`1990` per Rootstock reference data, or RCB admin user).

entries.explanation:
Field type: Picklist {Yes, No}, Optional (inherits from commodity code if blank).

Whether lot numbers are tracked at the item level.
transformations: Constant `No`. Override at item level only if RCB decides to lot-track specific consumables (inks).

entries.explanation:
Field type: Picklist {Yes, No}, Optional (inherits from commodity code if blank).

Whether serial numbers are tracked.
transformations: Constant `No` — cups/sleeves are not serialized.

entries.explanation:
Field type: Checkbox, Optional.

FIFO costing override at item level. Normally inherited from commodity code.
transformations: Leave NULL — inherit from commodity code.

entries.explanation:
Field type: Checkbox, Optional.

Reverse-BoM (disassembly) item flag.
transformations: Leave NULL — does not apply to RCB.

entries.explanation:
Field type: Checkbox, Optional.

Revision-controlled inventory tracking flag.
transformations: Leave NULL — does not apply to RCB.

entries.explanation:
Field type: Checkbox, Optional.

Multi-revision product flag.
transformations: Leave NULL — does not apply to RCB.

entries.explanation:
Field type: Lookup(Division Master), External ID, Required.

Eng Division for the commodity code record.
transformations: Constant `2` for all iccomcod rows.

entries.explanation:
Field type: Text(20), Required.

The commodity code name (primary identifier). One iccomcod row per code.
transformations:
Per-code value. Proposed set (11 codes):

Manufactured:
  • RCB-PRINT-CUP        — printed paper hot cups (P-WHC*, P-KIC*, P-CHC*, etc.)
  • RCB-PRINT-SLEEVE     — printed sleeves (P-DWS, P-DKS, P-CWS, P-CKS)
  • RCB-BLANK-CUP        — manufactured blank cups (WHC08/12/16/20, CHC*, B-CHC*, WSC22/32)
  • RCB-BLANK-SLEEVE     — manufactured blank sleeves (if any)

Purchased:
  • RCB-PRINT-MAT        — paper raw materials (PR-* paper sheets)
  • RCB-CONSUMABLE-INK   — inks (A0xxx)
  • RCB-CONSUMABLE-GLUE  — glues (D0xxx, C0xxx) — split from INK because operationally different
  • RCB-PACKAGING        — boxes, bags, tape, labels, printed instructions (BX-*, BG-*, BC*, N0*, TAPE-*, LABEL-*, BCI)
  • RCB-STOCK-RESALE     — warehoused stock for resale (Products.ProductGroupName = 'Warehoused')

Subcontract:
  • RCB-APPAREL-DROP     — drop-ship apparel (InvMasterSKU = 'OUTSOURCED', 1,275 SKUs)

Catch-all:
  • RCB-UNROUTED         — items that did not match any routing rule. Requires user review before load.

External IDs format as '2_<code>' (e.g., '2_RCB-PRINT-CUP') per the division prefix requirement.

entries.explanation:
Field type: Text(100), Required.

Human-readable description of the commodity code.
transformations:
Per-code value (human-readable):

  RCB-PRINT-CUP        → 'Printed Paper Hot Cups'
  RCB-PRINT-SLEEVE     → 'Printed Cup Sleeves'
  RCB-BLANK-CUP        → 'Manufactured Blank Cups'
  RCB-BLANK-SLEEVE     → 'Manufactured Blank Sleeves'
  RCB-PRINT-MAT        → 'Print Materials — Paper Stock'
  RCB-CONSUMABLE-INK   → 'Ink Consumables'
  RCB-CONSUMABLE-GLUE  → 'Glue Consumables'
  RCB-PACKAGING        → 'Packaging Materials (Boxes, Bags, Tape, Labels)'
  RCB-STOCK-RESALE     → 'Warehoused Stock for Resale'
  RCB-APPAREL-DROP     → 'Drop-Ship Apparel (Subcontract)'
  RCB-UNROUTED         → 'Items Requiring Review — Did Not Match Routing Rules'

entries.explanation:
Field type: Lookup(Manufacturing Users), External ID, Required.

Responsible inventory planner FK.
transformations: Placeholder/admin user ID (`1990` or RCB admin).

entries.explanation:
Field type: Lookup(Division Master), External ID, Required.

Buying Division FK.
transformations: Constant `2`.

entries.explanation:
Field type: Text(1), Required (typically A/B/C).

ABC inventory classification (A=high-value, B=mid, C=low).
transformations:
Per-code (educated guess; RCB should validate via velocity analysis):

  A — RCB-PRINT-CUP, RCB-PRINT-SLEEVE, RCB-BLANK-CUP, RCB-BLANK-SLEEVE (high-value finished/blank items)
  B — RCB-PRINT-MAT, RCB-STOCK-RESALE, RCB-APPAREL-DROP (mid-value)
  C — RCB-CONSUMABLE-INK, RCB-CONSUMABLE-GLUE, RCB-PACKAGING (low-value consumables)
  C — RCB-UNROUTED (default until reviewed)

entries.explanation:
Field type: Picklist {Pending, Active}, Required.

Lifecycle status of the commodity code.
transformations: Constant `Active`.

entries.explanation:
Field type: Picklist {Standard, Phantom, Reference}, Optional. NOTE: Schema doc omits this field but the import-template CSV includes it and the peitem schema explicitly references "the corresponding field on the Inventory Commodity Code" for Eng Type inheritance — confirming it exists..

Default Eng Type for items assigned to this commodity code.
